title: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 Downscaled Climate Projections (0.25°)
description: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 provides global daily climate projections at 0.25° statistically downscaled and bias-corrected with the BCSD method from CMIP6 global climate models, for the historical experiment (1950–2014) and four Tier 1 Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5; 2015–2100). Variables include precipitation, mean/maximum/minimum near-surface temperature, humidity, radiation and wind speed.
purpose: Offers a multi-model ensemble of daily climate scenarios at a common 0.25° grid for exploring projected changes in temperature, heat and precipitation over Algeria under different emission pathways.

spatial_extent.description: Global, 180°W–180°E, 60°S–90°N on a 0.25° grid (600 x 1440 cells). Files are global per model, scenario, variable and year; Algeria must be subset (e.g. via NCCS THREDDS NetcdfSubset).

temporal_extent.description: Historical experiment 1950–2014 and SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 for 2015–2100. Not all models provide all scenarios/variables (see Tech Note Appendix I). The AWS registry states no future updates are planned.

variables.name: pr
variables.description: Precipitation (mean of the daily precipitation rate)

variables.name: tas / tasmax / tasmin
variables.description: Daily mean, maximum and minimum near-surface air temperature

processing: Daily outputs of 35 CMIP6 GCM configurations were bias-corrected and spatially disaggregated (BCSD) against the 0.25° Global Meteorological Forcing Dataset (GMFD; Princeton Global Forcing) over 1960–2014 using quantile mapping, with temperature-trend preservation. Version 2.0 (Tech Note dated May 2025) applies bounds and fixes to v1.x outputs (e.g. hurs ≤ 105%, non-negative huss/rlds/sfcWind, adjustment of anomalously large values where daily climatology is very small).
limitations: BCSD assumes the 1960–2014 relative spatial patterns remain constant under future climate and adds no information beyond the parent CMIP6 runs other than resolution and bias correction.
BCSD adjusts the offset but not the slope of model trends; the Tech Note warns the linear shift may be unrealistic, particularly when using single GCMs.
The provider states the dataset is intended for scientific research and that engineering/design or commercial use is not recommended without expert consultation.

Earlier versions over-corrected precipitation in climatologically dry areas (reprocessed in v1.1) and could produce anomalously large values where daily climatology is very small (adjusted in v2.0); several file versions (v1.0, v1.1, v1.2, v2.0) coexist in the archive and must not be mixed.
The reference dataset GMFD is itself a reanalysis–observation blend; biases in GMFD over data-sparse regions propagate to all downscaled projections.

algeria_notes: At 0.25° (about 28 km) the Tell Atlas and coastal gradients are only partly resolved, and downscaled precipitation over the Algerian Sahara is very sensitive to BCSD behaviour where daily climatological rainfall is near zero (an issue the provider corrected in v1.1 and v2.0). Use ensembles rather than single models, compare SSPs, and treat percent-change precipitation signals over hyper-arid areas with caution.
